lead: This part turns the record into work. Fifteen packages between them carry every bottleneck in the register and every idea in Part 3. Each card says what the package is for, where it works, its first deliverable, how we will know it is done and what it waits on. Six can start today, six start the day I give my word, and three follow another package. Before you take one, read the box under the map: it holds the few rules that keep two people, two projects and one PC from getting in each other’s way.
mapShows: The left column needs no decision from me, no agents and no Docker gate for its first deliverable, so it can start today. The middle column waits on a word from me, and the right column on a deliverable of another package. WP2a’s side-by-side runs need only a quiet machine, so they can start sooner.
decLead: Every open decision with an id, in one place; go-aheads and permission yeses that have no id are on each card, under “Waiting on me”. Bold marks the option the source design recommends; where nothing is bold, there is no recommendation yet. I answered D01 to D06 on 11 November: yes to phase 1, an encrypted external drive for the copy, Docker’s start at sign-in stays off for now, no sleep on mains power, a sensor logger and a debugger are allowed, and sessions come back from a resume list two at a time. Only D05’s power-cut notes are still to come.
before: Each card says whether it works in FixFlow (this repository) or in the clinic testbed. Work on a branch, never on main. The ship plan and this compile live on the plan branch (PR #182), the knowledge-store design on PR #183’s branch and the skills on PR #185’s branch.

Before you use the Docker gate or start an agent, look at the lane board in `docs/program/W0-results.md` on the plan branch. If a FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer, harness work that needs the gate or agents waits.
One budget for the whole team

The two-lane cap and the written token budget (D07) are shared by all of us, not per person. Any Claude session that draws on my plan counts as one of the two lanes, your own working session included. Book agent runs in the shared queue and launch nothing on your own; WP11 sets the queue up first, and until it exists a run waits for my yes. The cap is for harness work; FixFlow’s lanes follow the ship plan’s own rule.

Both projects share this PC’s 31 GB [M] of memory, so a heavy check from either project takes a slot from FixFlow’s machine-wide lock, `ff-slot.sh`, like any FixFlow job. That lock is the one shared limit. Leave its pools and slot counts as they are; WP2b may propose how waiters are ordered, not how many run.
The coordinator writes FixFlow’s program files
A package that would change the ship plan, the lane board or FixFlow’s gate scripts sends a proposal to the coordinator. The coordinator brings it to me, and once I say go, the coordinator writes it.
Machine traps that already cost us time

Never prune Docker networks or restart Docker: other sessions run containers. Anything that needs its own Docker network gets an explicit subnet inside 10.77.0.0/16. With `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` set (the Git Bash setting that stops it rewriting paths), write paths as `C:/…`. Clone into scratch folders with git’s `core.longpaths` setting on (`git -c core.longpaths=true`), because Windows otherwise refuses long file paths. There is no `python` on PATH; our scripts run with Node. Never touch the antivirus.

packages.name: Machine and recovery
packages.mapLine: Copy off the PC, resume list, always-on logger
packages.worksIn: This PC and the clinic testbed repository; scripts and settings only, on a branch.
packages.goal: No power-off costs us work or a day. The work is copied off the PC every night, sessions come back from a resume list, and an always-on sensor logger records power, temperature and memory, so the next power-off can be diagnosed. This is harness v2 phase 1.
packages.first: Today: the bundle-and-verify script and the nightly copy script. They must also capture the six [M] folders in the clinic repository that are in no commit (register row B11) and the untracked harness documents. After I plug in and encrypt the drive, which comes after FixFlow’s P0a: the first verified copy.
packages.firstShort: Bundle-and-verify and nightly copy scripts; first verified copy after my drive step
packages.done: A clone from the copy shows the same heads, and the copy is never more than 24 hours old [T]. After one real reboot, done in a quiet window with my go, the resume list appears at sign-in with “start Docker” as its first line, and once Docker is up the databases in use are healthy within 3 minutes [T] with no further command. The next unexpected shutdown leaves a logger trace that ends at it.
packages.skills: Windows administration, PowerShell or bash scripting, git.
packages.size: One to two days of one session [E], scripts and settings only, no agents.
packages.depText: Needs nothing from another package. Mechanisms 7 and 8 (one fact, one command; a session parks itself when its record and branch disagree) come in here, because they cost one line in a brief.
packages.mine: Switch off sleep on mains power (D04); plug in the drive and switch on its encryption (D02); install the sensor logger and debugger (D05); write down the days the house lost power; say yes to the nightly copy as a scheduled task and to permission rules that deny agents the Railway commands `railway up` (deploys to the live host) and `railway run` (runs a command with the live settings); later, D08 (a battery backup) once the diagnosis is in. My steps come after FixFlow’s P0a.

packages.name: The clinic check
packages.mapLine: Container gate, slots from one number, heartbeat
packages.goal: One fast, fair and visible check for the clinic testbed: the Linux container run as the gate, check slots sized from one measured memory number, a queue that prints each check’s place, a heartbeat while it runs, and a reaper that lists what can be cleaned up. This is harness v2 phase 2.
packages.first: The container run and the Windows run side by side on recorded commits, with one check’s peak memory written down [M]. These runs need only a quiet machine, so they can start before WP1 is done. I decide D09 on that evidence.
packages.firstShort: Container and Windows runs side by side, with one check’s peak memory (can start sooner)
packages.done: Median gate near 230 s [T], zero Linux-only failures on main, no gap between heartbeats longer than 60 s [T], the next stall names its test, and after each merge the worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one.
packages.skills: Docker and Linux, test runners (pytest, Vitest, Jest), queues.
packages.size: Three to four days of one session [E], including one observed build day for the memory table. No agents.
packages.depText: The side-by-side runs and the one peak-memory figure need only a quiet machine. The memory table and any second slot need WP1’s logger and diagnosis first. The reaper only lists until I decide D10, and never touches a container, network or worktree that the clinic testbed’s own check and lane scripts did not create.
packages.mine: D09 (the container run as the gate), D10 (what may be cleaned up), and later D11 (who gives up memory).

packages.name: FixFlow’s gate harness and CI checks
packages.mapLine: Per-lane gates, fair slots, CI that can fail
packages.worksIn: FixFlow (this repository). Ship lanes use these scripts every day, so each change goes to the coordinator as a proposal and lands by atomic rename: the new script is written beside the old one and renamed over it in one step, so a running lane never reads a half-written script.
packages.goal: Keep FixFlow’s own gates fast, fair and honest: the per-lane gate harness and slot lock the ship lanes use, a gate that mirrors CI, and CI checks that fail when they should and never pass a run that tested nothing.
packages.first: Gate waits measured per lane under the new ticket queue, and a negative run proving the CI checks fail when they should: skipped integration tests fail the job, and Jest never runs with `--passWithNoTests`.
packages.firstShort: Gate waits per lane measured; a negative run proving CI fails when it should
packages.done: Every gate kind takes the per-lane lock first, Node failures are re-run under Node 22 before they are called defects, and a planted skip or an empty test run turns CI red once the new checks have run record-only over recent merges.
packages.skills: Bash, Docker, GitHub Actions, pytest and Jest.
packages.size: A day or two per item [G]. The changes are small; the care is in not disturbing running lanes.
packages.depText: Needs nothing from another package. It starts on my word because the coordinator owns these scripts while ship lanes run.
packages.mine: My go, through the coordinator, before any change to `ff-gates.sh` or `ff-slot.sh`.

packages.name: Gate, review and merge scripts
packages.mapLine: Sealed replay, transcript audit, merge queue
packages.worksIn: The clinic testbed’s recorded history, read only, and a scripts folder on a branch of the clinic testbed repository. Changes to FixFlow’s review practice are proposals to the coordinator.
packages.goal: Move the mechanical part of review and merging out of the orchestrating session into scripts that spend no tokens: a sealed replay, a verdict script, a transcript audit at merge, one finding table, a dry run with stand-in agents and a merge queue that checks who read the final commit. Then the gate workflow, where the reviewers run outside the orchestrating session, and the fix-round contract. This is harness v2 phase 3.
packages.first: The replay seal (mechanism 1: a script that builds a sealed clone at a recorded commit, with no agent) and the transcript audit (mechanism 3). Building both costs no tokens and no check time, so they can start today on the recorded data; the seal’s own two-run test books its agents under D07.
packages.firstShort: Replay seal and transcript audit, on the record
packages.done: Each of the six scripts (sealed replay, verdict script, transcript audit, finding table, dry run with stand-in agents, merge queue) passes the test the harness v2 design sets for it (§4), and the merge queue has run record-only over the 65 [M] recorded merges and flagged the unread final heads of 10 and 11 November by itself. A script refuses a merge only after I say so (D15).
packages.skills: Scripting, git internals, test tooling, careful diff reading.
packages.size: About a week of one session for the scripts [E].
packages.depText: The verdict script re-runs the cited tests, which takes check time, so it is easier after WP2a and runs only in a quiet window. The fix-round contract comes after the seal and the verdict script.
packages.mine: D12 to D20, each as its mechanism reaches me. D13 (one reports folder) and D17 (hooks) are permission changes.

packages.name: Planner and lanes
packages.mapLine: Lane count below the knee, no file collisions
packages.worksIn: Reads FixFlow’s ship plan §7 and its lane board and never edits them. Its output is a recommendation the coordinator may adopt.
packages.goal: Know before a wave starts which slices can run side by side, how many lanes are worth it and where they would collide: the planner, the scheduler and the plan check of harness v2, measured against how FixFlow already runs its lanes.
packages.first: The plan check replayed on FixFlow’s first lane wave, whose lanes declared the files they own (ship plan §7.3): the collision graph and the lane count it would have chosen.
packages.firstShort: Plan check replayed on FixFlow’s first lane wave
packages.done: It runs record-only on the next wave first, and sets the lane count only after the coordinator and I accept it.
packages.skills: Graphs and scheduling, scripting, a feel for queues.
packages.depText: Needs WP8’s first deliverable, the rate sheet: the planner reads its rates from there. Easier after WP2a, because check capacity is one of the limits it plans against.
packages.mine: Accepting its recommendation, together with the coordinator.

packages.name: Token budget
packages.mapLine: Written budget per window; the four levers
packages.worksIn: Transcripts on this PC, read only, and Claude Code settings, for both projects.
packages.goal: Give every wave a written token budget, build the governor that slows lanes so the five-hour window lasts, and put the four levers from the token report to work: (1) cap long windows, (2) shrink the fixed start every agent re-reads, (3) batch lookups, and (4) stop the model’s own output piling up in its window.

packages.firstShort: D07 budget proposal from the saved baseline

packages.name: The library and lesson memory
packages.mapLine: Limitations first, then a held-out pilot
packages.worksIn: Design documents in `docs/program/` and the clinic testbed’s recorded runs. Nothing is built until the limitation list is agreed.
packages.goal: Give the harness a memory a cheaper model can use: the reasoning-cache library of harness v2, written when something becomes true and asked for, never pushed. We agree what can go wrong before we choose any fix.
packages.first: The library’s limitation list agreed with me, with the pathway map’s two weights for each limitation (alone, and as the last one left).
packages.done: A pilot on held-out work measures whether a session that asks the library first reads less and gets more right, under the frozen validation contract.

packages.name: The knowledge store (PR #183)
packages.mapLine: Recurrence audit, then my second yes
packages.worksIn: FixFlow’s history, read only, for the audit; the design on PR #183’s branch. Its phases always yield to ship phases.
packages.goal: Build, if the audit says it would pay, the knowledge store designed in PR #183: a store of hard solved problems, traps and do-not-apply facts, looked up by pull only, and stale when its code changes, never by age.
packages.first: The recurrence audit (KS-0), which writes no code: one Sonnet session and an Opus refuter count the repeats a store could have served. It runs under D07, books its place in the shared queue and waits while a FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer.

packages.name: Docs that stay true to the code

decisions.q: FixFlow’s P0a, my own steps in the ship plan
decisions.options: **Do P0a first; my harness steps follow it, except the notes and decisions marked now**
decisions.unblocks: every step of mine below that is not marked now

decisions.q: The power-cut notes
decisions.when: now (the rest of D05 is answered)
decisions.options: **Write down the days the house lost power**

decisions.q: What is the token budget per five-hour window?
decisions.when: before the first run that launches agents
decisions.options: **Start from the one measured window (about 3.4 million subagent tokens [M]) and adjust once the per-slice tally is rerun on November’s transcripts** / Set my own figure

decisions.q: If the mains is the cause: a battery backup?
decisions.options: **Decide when the diagnosis is in** / Buy one now

decisions.q: Make the Linux container run the gate?
decisions.options: **Yes; Windows runs only when the Windows-side tools change** / Run both on every gate / Keep Windows as the gate

decisions.q: What may be cleaned up, and by whom?
decisions.options: **The reaper lists; I approve each batch** / Automatic for merged and clean worktrees after 24 quiet hours / Leave as it is

decisions.q: Who gives up memory?
decisions.options: One shared test database / A cap on the WSL2 machine / Close other applications during builds

decisions.q: Which findings get a second look, and when does a finding go stale?
decisions.options: **Second look only at money, stock, access, import and restore; a finding goes stale when the code it points at changes, never by age** / Second look at all of them

decisions.q: May agents write reports to one folder without asking?
decisions.options: **Allow one reports folder, after a write probe of twenty short runs passes** / Keep asking each time

decisions.q: May the script’s verdict replace the root’s own reading?
decisions.options: **Side by side for one wave, then decide** / Replace now / Never; the root reads every diff

decisions.q: May a script merge, edit the board and refuse?
decisions.options: **Record-only over the recorded merges first, then refuse on high-risk branches** / Refuse on every branch / Flag only, never refuse

decisions.q: Will I read the marked lines of high-risk merges?
decisions.options: **Try it on three merges and log the wait** / Skip

decisions.q: Do hooks stay off?
decisions.options: **Stay off** / Re-open them for two uses: a stop hook that blocks a session on a failed claim check, and a heartbeat fed by tool events

decisions.q: A short tool list for gate agents?
decisions.options: **Adopt only on a measured drop** / Skip

decisions.q: A second vendor’s model in the review replay?
decisions.options: **Not now; run the same-model arm only** / Approve, after the sealed replay exists

decisions.q: Replay three candidate fixes per recorded chain?
decisions.options: **Not yet; decide after the contract’s replay** / Run it once the seal exists

decisions.q: What must the index replay show?
decisions.options: The marks a refuter suggested: 3 % of tokens and a recall of 0.8 [T] / Set my own marks / Skip the replay

decisions.q: Rehearse on a real host?
decisions.options: **Free steps with me present (restore, deploy checklist, off-site push and a planted alert), then rent a host for a day** / Free steps only, for now / Wait

decisions.q: Try the earlier compaction window?
decisions.options: **Try it on one wave, and call the result an anecdote** / Skip; work on one phase per session and a smaller pre-read first

decisions.q: Run the knowledge store’s recurrence audit (KS-0)?
decisions.when: now, never ahead of a ship phase
decisions.options: **Yes** / Not now

decisions.q: Build the knowledge store?
decisions.options: **Not until the audit is in; then ask me again** / Build now

decisions.q: The library’s limitation list
decisions.options: **Agree the list before any fix is chosen**

decisions.q: Put an agent in the loop of the graph test?
decisions.options: **After the zero-token index replay, under a written budget** / Now / Not at all

decisions.q: Installs for the wider graph test: a graph database server, graphify, an embedding model
decisions.options: Each one when its arm is scheduled / None for now

decisions.q: Merge PR #185 (skills and agents)?
decisions.options: Merge after the review / Hold
